abs_err_delay_40ns.description: THE SLACK CLAIM, spent in one place -- UNCHANGED bound, carried over from the five-loop sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/ deck (issue #311). Re-checks that the ~40 ns margin spec/prior-art-survey.md Sec 4.2 budgets is really available, with real gf180mcu logic (not ideal XSPICE primitives) implementing the sequencer that has to consume its own share of that margin between the comparator decision and the next latching edge.

notes: ISSUE #311 PER-LOOP DECOMPOSITION: this experiment is one of five (`sar-logic-timing-gates-ok/-lt/-xl/-bad/-tie`) split out of the single five-loop sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/ deck. The measurement definitions, bounds and 8.5 us duration are UNCHANGED; only how many loops share one ngspice deck changed. Rationale, the cost measurement that motivated it, and the 'five slugs vs one deck-variant axis' decision are in sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/investigations/20260917-issue-303-five-loop-composition-cost.md and design/sar-logic/flow/gen_sar_ctrl_gates_tb.py's own module docstring ('Per-loop timing decomposition (issue #311)').

COMPUTATIONAL COST: not independently measured for this loop's own delayed-comparator-plus-T-line composition (`cmp_delay=40n`); it is structurally the same closed loop as `ok` (same controller/CDAC size, same 8.5 us duration, one loop per deck) plus a matched-50-ohm transmission line, so it is expected to cost about the same order as `ok`'s measured ~132 core-s per point (sim/sar-logic-timing-gates-ok/testbench/tb.json). A run's own record states the actual measured per-point cost.
The delay value (40 ns) is the SAME bisected bracket point the rung-1 ideal sibling and the five-loop gate-level deck use -- this record re-checks that bracket, it does not re-derive it.

The behavioural CDAC/comparator model and start-pulse seeding (design/sar-logic/rtl/README.md's 'Real hardware note') are UNCHANGED from the five-loop deck -- only the loop composition changed. Issue #296's comparator-output-slew fix does NOT apply to this loop: `lt`'s comparator drives a matched 50 ohm terminated transmission line, not a bare gate input, so it was never subject to the zero-time-step abort #296 fixed (see design/sar-logic/flow/gen_sar_ctrl_gates_tb.py's 'Comparator output slew' section).

What this record does NOT claim: no place-and-route, no STA/timing closure (DR-0023 follow-ons (b)/(c), issues #274/#275) -- this is a pre-layout gate-level netlist wrapped directly in SPICE, with no extracted parasitics and no real interconnect delay. It is also not evidence about real CDAC settling or comparator behaviour.
